title: A Sigil for the Salt
premise: Ada Nystrom's gift lets her steal memories as physical sigils, and she has survived the Thornfell smuggler roads by selling fragments of other people's pasts. When the crown declares a hunt for all memory-wielders, Ada learns her gift is not a curse but a fragment of the Salt Covenant, a broken pact between the human realm and the drowned kingdom beneath Thornfell's lakes. Hunted by the crown's inquisitor—her former lover, Captain Emeric Vale—Ada must gather seven scattered covenant sigils, each hidden inside a stolen memory she herself took years ago. In the end, Ada discovers she is the living seal of the covenant: to reforge it she must surrender every memory of who she loves, including Emeric, choosing duty over self and becoming the bridge between realms.
about_author: Astrid Okonkwo is a former archivist who grew up between coastal fishing towns and inland mountain villages, a duality that haunts her fiction. She writes fantasy about people whose gifts cost them something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Ada Nystrom lifts a merchant's memory of his dead daughter from a Thornfell waystation, feeling the familiar guilt of trading grief for coin. Her POV establishes her gift, her rules, and her loneliness. The emotional beat is quiet unease—she steals memories but keeps none of her own childhood.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Greywater Ford
chapters.summary: In the market town of Greywater Ford, criers announce the crown's hunt for memory-wielders, and Ada watches an old hedge-witch dragged away. POV shifts briefly to Captain Emeric Vale, who recognizes a thief's mark on the crowd. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve as Ada flees into the mountains.

chapters.title: What the Lake Remembers
chapters.summary: Hiding in a smuggler cave above Lake Vess, Ada touches the water and hears it speak—a memory older than any human. The lake names her 'seal-bearer' and shows her the first covenant sigil glowing inside one of her own stolen memories. Beat: wonder colliding with dread.

chapters.title: The Drowned Court's Envoy
chapters.summary: A drowned-kingdom envoy named Sef rises from the lake, half-salmon, half-mournful courtier, demanding Ada restore the covenant before the spring thaw floods the lowlands. Ada refuses; she is a thief, not a savior. Beat: defiance masking terror at what the task will demand of her.

chapters.title: Seven Sigils, One Thief
chapters.summary: Sef explains the covenant's structure: seven sigils scattered when the pact broke, each lodged in a memory Ada stole during her lost childhood. Emeric's hunting party enters the mountains behind them. Beat: reluctant bargain struck under pursuit pressure.

chapters.title: The First Memory: Ash on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Ada opens her own hidden cache and relives burning the granary at Hollowmere—the night the covenant broke, which she witnessed as a child and stole from herself to survive. The first sigil emerges. Beat: horror at discovering she caused the catastrophe she must repair.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Road
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV: interrogating a captured smuggler, he pieces together that the thief he's chasing is Ada, the woman he loved before she vanished five years ago. His loyalty to the crown wars with his heart. Beat: bitter tenderness sharpening the hunt.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Whispers
chapters.summary: Ada and Sef barter passage through a tollhouse where a blind keeper trades in secrets. Ada pays with a precious memory of her mother's lullaby to learn the second sigil's location. Beat: sacrifice establishing the price of the quest.

chapters.title: Salt in the Snowfield
chapters.summary: Crossing the high snowfields, they recover the second sigil from a frozen shrine, but Emeric's riders ambush them. Sef is wounded by blessed iron; Ada uses a stolen soldier's memory to turn the squad against itself. Beat: first blood, guilt deepening.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sheltering with Ada's old fence, Maro, she discovers someone sold her name to the crown—and the ledger implicates Maro himself. She spares him but takes his memory of their friendship as payment. Beat: betrayal and cold pragmatism costing her another piece of warmth.

chapters.title: Emeric at the Fireline
chapters.summary: Emeric corners Ada alone at a forest firebreak. Instead of arresting her, he demands the truth; she gives him a stolen memory showing the crown's own role in breaking the covenant. Beat: love against duty made flesh—he lets her go and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Third and Fourth
chapters.summary: Ada retrieves two sigils in quick succession—from a drowned chapel and a mad hermit who guards the fourth willingly, begging to forget. She realizes the sigils were never lost; they were hidden by people who couldn't bear them. Beat: the quest reframes as mercy.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV shift to Lord Chancellor Ives, who knows the covenant can be reforged—but only if the crown controls the seal. He orders Emeric to capture Ada alive, revealing the hunt was engineered to flush her out. Beat: the true villain surfaces.

chapters.title: Sinking the Fifth
chapters.summary: Sef leads Ada beneath Lake Vess to the drowned court, where the fifth sigil rests on the Sunken Throne. The dying king offers her power if she seals the covenant in the drowned realm's favor. Beat: temptation—she could choose a side instead of a balance.

chapters.title: What Ada Stole From Herself
chapters.summary: Recovering the sixth sigil forces Ada to relive the memory she stole first: her mother was a covenant-keeper, executed by the crown, and child-Ada broke the pact trying to save her. Beat: identity shattered and rebuilt—she understands why she became a thief.

chapters.title: Maro's Price
chapters.summary: Maro, seeking redemption, sells Ives false information and is executed for it; his death buys Ada time to reach the final sigil site. She carries his last memory like a stone. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Seventh Sigil Is a Person
chapters.summary: At the covenant's origin-stone, Ada learns the seventh sigil lives in Emeric—he was born a covenant-warden without knowing it. To complete the rite, both must stand at the stone as the thaw begins. Beat: the lovers' fates entwined against their wills.

chapters.title: Chains of Office
chapters.summary: Ives captures Emeric and uses him as bait, staging a public execution at the origin-stone to force Ada's hand. Ada walks into the trap openly, sigils blazing. Beat: courage replacing cunning as stealth fails.

chapters.title: Climax: The Rite at the Origin-Stone
chapters.summary: As floodwaters rise, Ada begins the rite while Emeric breaks free to shield her; Ives tries to seize the covenant's power and is unmade by truths he cannot bear. Six sigils burn—but the seventh requires a willing surrender of love. Beat: everything converges.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Emeric, understanding what the rite will take, chooses to give his memories of Ada freely so the covenant can bind. She accepts, weeping, and gives hers in return. Beat: the theme resolved—love proven by its sacrifice, not its possession.

chapters.title: The Seal-Bearer
chapters.summary: The covenant reforges: waters recede, the drowned court sleeps in peace, and Ada becomes the living seal—a woman with no past, known to both realms. Emeric, remembering nothing, salutes the stranger who saved the world. Beat: bittersweet transcendence.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Salt
chapters.summary: Months later, a memory-thief works the roads again, stealing pain from the grieving for free. At Lake Vess she pauses, feeling an ache she cannot name, and the water whispers a name: Emeric. Beat: hope—some bonds outlast memory, and perhaps love can be relearned.
